body.html: Huandalha Resort sits at 118 Moo 15, Pa Sak, Mueang Lamphun — still within Mueang district, a few minutes' drive from the town centre. It is about 5 km from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and roughly 20 km from Chiang Mai Airport, so Lamphun makes an easy base for visiting both towns. The resort sits near a main road, which makes it easy to find — but rooms on the road side do catch traffic noise, so light sleepers should ask for a garden-side room set back from the road.

What guests mention most is that the rooms are more spacious than you would expect for the price. They are single-storey, arranged around a garden, with single, twin (two single beds) and double options. Inside there is fast-cooling air-con, a fridge, an LCD TV, and — the bit many like — a small in-room kitchenette to boil water or reheat food, handy for longer stays or saving on meals. The large bathroom is another point reviews praise. Decor is simple for the price — nothing fancy, but clean and complete.
"Very spacious room, big bathroom too, air-con cools fast, and the little in-room kitchenette is handy. Friendly, helpful staff and great value for Lamphun."

On facilities, it covers the essentials on a budget. There is an on-site restaurant, a massage room, a garden to stroll, free parking, free Wi-Fi, laundry service and a front desk. Self-drivers like the easy parking and that the resort is simple to find, being near the main road. Breakfast is local-style and served in the morning (charged separately). There is no swimming pool, so if you are set on a swim, look at other options in this list alongside it. Overall it leans on spacious, good-value rooms rather than luxury facilities.

On scores, Huandalha Resort earns steady praise for room size and value. Trip.com rates it around 7.7 from 19 reviews, and Tripadvisor around 3.3 out of 5. It scores well on room size, cleanliness, friendly staff, and prices starting in the low ฿800s — good value for a room this size with a kitchenette built in. Across platforms, the consensus is that it suits travellers who want value and a roomy base to relax in.

There are a few things to know before booking. Because it sits near a main road, road-side rooms catch traffic noise, especially trucks at night — light sleepers should request a garden-side room. A few reviews mention construction or refurbishment noise at certain times, and limited flexibility on house rules, so confirm the terms when you book. The resort is plain and simple, with no pool, and it is not in a walkable old-town strip — most dinners and cafes mean a drive into town. If you expect a boutique feel or brand-new fittings, set expectations to the price.

In short, Huandalha Resort suits travellers who want a spacious, clean room with a kitchenette, in the low-฿800s, a quiet garden setting, and still close to central Lamphun. If you are driving, staying several nights, or want to save on meals with the in-room kitchenette, it fits well. If you want to walk to old-town restaurants and cafes, need a pool, prefer a boutique style, or are bothered by traffic noise, look at in-town options alongside it.

A tip from following the reviews here: ask for a garden-side room set back from the road — it is much quieter at night. On longer stays, the in-room kitchenette genuinely saves on meals, so bring some dry goods or shop at Lamphun's market. Set the resort's GPS pin before you arrive for an easy approach. During temple festivals and merit-making days at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai rooms fill fast, so book ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate first.

faq.q: Where is Huandalha Resort and what is nearby?
faq.a: It is at 118 Moo 15, Pa Sak, Mueang Lamphun, still within Mueang district, about 8–10 minutes' drive from the town centre · about 5 km from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai · roughly 2.4 km from Hariphunchai Golf Club · about 20 km (around 30 minutes) from Chiang Mai town and airport · the resort is near a main road, so it is easy to find — set GPS before you arrive.

faq.q: How much does Huandalha Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: From approx. ฿800/night for a Deluxe Single · a Deluxe Double with a double bed is around ฿900, and a Deluxe Twin with two beds around ฿1,000 · all rooms are spacious with a small kitchenette, fridge, LCD TV, air-con and free Wi-Fi · prices move with the season and festivals, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Huandalha Resort?
faq.a: Rooms are single-storey, set around a garden, and larger than expected for the price · they have a small kitchenette, fridge, LCD TV, fast-cooling air-con and a big bathroom · decor is simple for the price, clean and complete · reviewers mainly praise the room size and the value.

faq.q: Does it have a swimming pool and what facilities are there?
faq.a: There is no swimming pool · there is an on-site restaurant, a massage room, a garden to stroll, free parking, free Wi-Fi, laundry service and a front desk · rooms have a small kitchenette, fridge and TV · it covers the essentials on a budget rather than luxury facilities.

faq.q: Who is Huandalha Resort best for?
faq.a: Best for self-drivers, longer stays or value-minded travellers who want a spacious room with a kitchenette and a quiet garden setting, close to central Lamphun · less suited to those who want to walk to old-town restaurants and cafes, need a pool, prefer a boutique style, or are bothered by traffic noise from the main road.

faq.q: Is it noisy, and does it really have an in-room kitchen?
faq.a: Because it is near a main road, road-side rooms catch traffic noise, especially trucks at night — ask for a garden-side room set back from the road for a much quieter night · and yes, most rooms do have a small in-room kitchenette and fridge to boil water or reheat food, handy for longer stays or saving on meals.
